METHODS 
The 2027 Bristol Bay sockeye salmon forecast is the sum of individual predictions from nine river 
systems  (Kvichak,  Alagnak,  Naknek,  Egegik,  Ugashik,  Wood,  Igushik,  Nushagak,  and  Togiak  
Rivers)  and  four  age  classes  (ages  1.2,  1.3,  2.2,  and  2.3).  Adult  escapement  and  return  data  from  
brood years 1972–2021 were used in the analyses for most rivers. 
Forecasts  for  each  age  class  returning  to  a  river  system  were  derived  from  models  based  on  the  
relationship between adult returns of that age class and either total returns or sibling returns from the 
same brood years. The average return over the last five years was also considered as a forecast model, 
and  in  certain  cases,  competing  models  were  averaged  in  a  weighted  hybrid  model  approach.  In 
general,  models  with  statistically  significant  parameters  and/or  the  best  past  performance  metrics 
were  chosen.  Performance  was  evaluated  using  mean  absolute  deviation,  mean  absolute  percent  
error,  mean  arctangent  absolute  percent  error,  and  mean  percent  error  between  forecasted  and

2026 BRISTOL BAY SALMON SEASON SUMMARY REVISED 
 
The following is an overview of the 2026 Bristol Bay commercial salmon season. A ll data are preliminary. 
Revised  information  is  highlighted  in  bold.  The  2026 inshore  Bristol  Bay  sockeye  salmon  run  of  45.7 
million  fish  (Table  1)  was 8%  below  the 49.6 million average  run  for  the  latest  20-year  period  (2006–
2025; Vega et    al.  2026). This is the first year since 2014 that the total inshore run was less than 50 million 
fish. 
The 2026 Bristol Bay sockeye salmon run was 4% above the preseason inshore forecast of 44.1 million 
fish (Table 2)  . All sockeye salmon escapement goals were met or exceeded, except for the Togiak River, 
which did not meet the lower bound of the escapement goal. Baywide escapement totaled 15.6 million 
fish (Table 3). The commercial harvest of 30.1 million sockeye salmon was 7% below the 32.3 million 
preseason forecast (Table 1; Weaver and Terry-Shindelman 2025). The preliminary harvest estimates for 
other species are 10,700 Chinook, 457,100 chum, 55,100 coho, and 666,700 pink salmon (Table 1). 
 
EXVESSEL VALUE 
Exvessel value of all salmon species caught in Bristol Bay in 2026 was estimated using price information 
from processor final  operations  reports,  and  numbers  and  average  weights  from  preliminary  fish  ticket  
numbers. The 2026 Bristol Bay preliminary exvessel value of $264.0 million for all salmon species (Table 
4) was 21%  above  the  20-year  average  of  $207.8    million  (Vega et  al.   2026).   Prices may  not  include 
incentives for icing, bleeding, floating, or production bonuses.  
 
SPECIES PERFORMANCE 
Sockeye Salmon  
The 2026 harvest of 30.1 million sockeye salmon was 14% lower than the recent 20-year average of 34.9 
million (Table 5; Vega et al.  2026). Sockeye salmon escapement goals were exceeded on the Nushagak, 
Igushik and Ugashik Rivers. The Togiak River escapement was below the lower bound escapement goal 
range. The Kvichak, Naknek, Alagnak, Egegik, and Wood rivers were within their escapement goal ranges 
(Table 3). Baywide run timing was two days early compared to the 20-year average.  
In  2026, the age  composition  of  sockeye  salmon  in  Bristol  Bay  was roughly  on forecast,  with  45%  2-

This is the Alaska Department of Fish and Game in Dillingham with an announcement regarding 
commercial fishing in the Togiak District. This is Westside Salmon Announcement number 31

Togiak District next week.

gather additional information.

items.title: BRISTOL BAY 2026 SALMON FISHERY UPDATE #2
items.text:
This is the Alaska Department of Fish & Game in King Salmon and Dillingham with an 
update for permit holders and subsistence users in all Bristol Bay salmon fishing districts. 
The time is 3:00 p.m., and the date is Thursday, July 9, 2026.  
 
This  update  is  to  announce  that the  new  regulations  adopted  by  the  Alaska  Board  of  
Fisheries in January 2026 that modified the Bristol Bay salmon fisheries (5 AAC 06.001–
5 AAC 06.391) will be in effect starting July 12, 2026. 
 
The following summarizes Board adopted changes:   
  
Baywide 
• Board adopted vessel specifications and operations (5 AAC 06.341).   
 
Ugashik District 
• In the Ugashik Village subdistrict, the set gillnet offshore distance described in 5 AAC 
06.331(m)(8) will be 1,000 feet. 
 
Nushagak District 
• Mandatory retention of king salmon caught in the Nushagak District. King salmon may 
not be retained for personal use and must either be sold or donated.  
• The set gillnet area lines described in 5 AAC 06.331(n)(2)–   (4) will take effect. 
• Required distance between drift and set gillnet gear (5 AAC 06.335)(c)(1 and 2)-  no 
part  of  a  drift  gillnet  operation  may  contact  any  part  of  a  set  gillnet  operation  in  the  
Nushagak District. 
 
Togiak District 
• The department will open the Kulukak Section by emergency order beginning July 13 
(5 AAC 06.320(a)(2)). Expect an announcement on July 12. 
• he  department  may  now  extend  fishing  in  the  Togiak  Bay  Section  by  more  than  48  
hours if warranted (5 AAC 06.369(c)(3)).

items.text:
This is the Alaska Department of Fish & Game in King Salmon and Dillingham with an update for permit 
holders and subsistence users in all Bristol Bay salmon fishing districts. The time is 9:00 a.m., and the date 
is Friday, June 5, 2026.  
This update is intended to clarify how the Bristol Bay salmon fishery will be managed at the start of the 
2026 season and serves as a supplement to the Commercial Salmon Fishing Outlook released on March 
23, 2026. New regulations adopted by the Alaska Board of Fisheries in January 2026 that modified the 
Bristol Bay salmon fisheries (5 AAC 06.001–5 AAC 06.391) are still undergoing review by the Alaska 
Department of Law, therefore fisheries will be managed consistent with the existing codified regulations 
until the new regulations become effective 30 days after they are filed by the Lieutenant Governor.  
 
The  current  codified  Bristol  Bay  Subsistence,  Commercial  Salmon  and  Herring,  and  Statewide  
Regulations (5 AAC 06.001–5 AAC 06.391) are available at:  
https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/static/regulations/fishregulations/pdfs/commercial/cf_bristolbay_2023_202
6.pdf 
 
The department will use its Emergency Order (EO) authority to implement regulations specific to king 
salmon conservation. Provisions of the Nushagak District King Salmon Stock of Concern Management 
Plan, including the new king salmon triggers, will be applied during the 2026 season. Management actions 
for  Nushagak  District  king  salmon,  as  outlined  in  the  March  Outlook,  remain  in  place  and  will  guide  
inseason decision-making. 
 
The following Board-adopted changes will not be in effect at the start of the season, as indicated in the 
March Outlook, but may become effective midseason once filed and after the 30-day notice period: 
    
Baywide 
• Board adopted vessel specifications and operations (5 AAC 06.341) reverts to the 2025 
regulations. 

 
Ugashik District 
• In the Ugashik Village subdistrict, the set gillnet offshore distance described in 5 AAC 
06.331 (m)(8) reverts to the 2025 regulation of 800 feet. 
Nushagak District 
• Requirements  for  the  mandatory  retention  of  king  salmon  caught  in  the  Nushagak  
District  and  the  further  requirement  that  those  fish  be  sold  or  donated  and  not  be  
retained for personal use will not be in effect to start the season. 
• The set gillnet lines described in 5 AAC 06.331(n)(2)–(4) revert to the 2022 regulations 
because of the sunset clause (v). That means (2) would be 500 feet from the mean high 
tide mark,  (3) would be 700 feet from the mean high tide mark, and (4) would be 1,000 
feet from the mean high tide mark. 
• Required distance between drift and set gillnet gear (5 AAC 06.335) reverts to 2025 
regulations. 
Togiak District 
• The fishing schedule in Kulukak Section (5 AAC 06.320(a)(2)) reverts to Monday 9:00 
a.m. until Wednesday 9:00 p.m. 
•  T he change regarding the 48-hour maximum extension (5 AAC 06.369(c)(3)) reverts 
to the 2025 regulation.

stand by at    regular announcement times: 9:00 a.m., 12:00 noon, 3:00 p.m., 6:00 p.m., and 8:00 p.m., unless 
otherwise  stated.  Information  is  also  available  via  telephone:  for  eastside  fisheries  (Naknek-Kvichak, 
Egegik, and Ugashik), dial 907-246-INFO (4636); for westside fisheries (Nushagak and Togiak), dial 907-
842-5226. Regular office hours at the Dillingham (Alaska Department of Fish and Game; ADF&G) office 
will be 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, except from June 17 through July 17, the office 
will  be  open  seven  days  a  week  from  8:00  a.m.  to  5:00  p.m.  In  King  Salmon,  the  office  hours  are  as  
follows: June 1 to June 17 and after July 17: 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., and 1:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed 
for lunch and weekends. From June 17 through July 17: 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., seven days per week.  
ADF&G Forms 
All relevant Bristol Bay forms are available online and can be submitted in various ways,  including by 
email. Contacts are listed on ADF&G's Bristol Bay home page, here:  
https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/index.cfm?adfg=commercialbyareabristolbay.contacts 
To avoid problems and processing delays, please submit forms early. Contact your processor for a digital 
copy  of  your  Permit  Holder's  Agent  Authorization  (PHAA)  form.  Set  gillnet  permit  holders  are  only  
required to fill out and return set gillnet registration cards if they fish in the Nushagak District. Drift gillnet 
permit holders must fill out and return district registration cards prior to commercial fishing in any district 
in Bristol Bay. PDF files of district registration cards, permit holder agent authorization forms, and dual 
drift   registration   forms   are   posted   online   on   the   department   Bristol   Bay   homepage   here: 
https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/index.cfm?adfg=commercialbyareabristolbay.salmon#management and can 
be  printed,  completed,  then  mailed  to  the  address  on  the  printout,  or  submitted  electronically  to  
DFG.BristolBay.CF.Forms@alaska.gov.  If  electronic  or  mail  submission  is  not  possible,  forms  will  be  
available from and may be submitted to Anchorage, King Salmon, or Dillingham office personnel.  

Crewmember  licenses  may  be  difficult  to  obtain  in  Bristol  Bay  and  crewmembers  should  buy  licenses  
before arriving. They are available through the ADFG app or online, here: 
https://www.adfg.alaska.gov/index.cfm?adfg=fishlicense.crewmember
